title: Pull out the greatest common factor
subtitle: Equivalent expressions · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Equivalent expressions are this one** — 14 Easy, 2 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The given expression is a sum of two or three terms whose coefficients share a number, and often a power of x.
- Every choice is written as something times a bracket, so the question is really asking what the common factor is.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the GCF of the coefficients and the lowest power of each variable that every term shares.
- 2) Divide each term by that GCF to get what goes in the bracket.
- 3) Quick check: multiply the choice back out in your head.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph the original and a choice.
Matching curves confirm it, but it's faster to multiply the choice back out mentally, because these are easy questions.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pull out a factor that isn't the greatest (the choice looks right but can still be factored).
Or you forget to lower the exponent on the variable in each term, or drop a term whose quotient is 1.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You pull out a factor that isn't the greatest (the choice looks right but can still be factored).
Or you forget to lower the exponent on the variable in each term, or drop a term whose quotient is 1.
